sections.label: Air Navigation Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Air Navigation Act to meet new international civil aviation obligations and enhance penalties for unmanned aircraft offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We need to update the Act from time to time to ensure that our regulatory framework keeps pace with developments in the aviation sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This Air Navigation (Amendment) Bill amends ANA to enable Singapore to meet new international civil aviation obligations and to enhance penalties for a greater deterrent effect for offences involving unmanned aircraft.

sections.label: CAAS permits approved in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, CAAS approved 522 Operator Permits and 2,322 Activity Permits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In 2018, CAAS approved 522 Operator Permits and 2,322 Activity Permits.

sections.label: Unmanned aircraft registration regime
sections.summary: CAAS is introducing mandatory registration for all unmanned aircraft above 250 grammes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: CAAS is tightening this unmanned aircraft regulatory framework by introducing a mandatory registration regime for all unmanned aircraft above 250 grammes (g).

sections.label: Current unmanned aircraft offence penalty
sections.summary: The penalty for most unmanned aircraft offences is currently a maximum fine of $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Today, the penalty for most of the offences involving unmanned aircraft is a maximum fine of $20,000.

sections.label: Increased penalties for unmanned aircraft offences
sections.summary: The Bill introduces jail terms and raises fines for various unmanned aircraft offences, including up to $100,000 or 10 years for endangering life or property.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For the offence of conducting any aerial activity without the required aviation safety instruments, such as operating an unmanned aircraft without the required operator and/or activity permits, the Bill introduces a discretionary jail term of up to two years for first offenders, and up to five years for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For the offence of operating an unmanned aircraft to overfly or take photographs of a protected area, or discharging a substance, whether gaseous, liquid or solid, without authorisation when flying an unmanned aircraft, the Bill raises the maximum fine for first offenders from $20,000 to $50,000 and raises or introduces a jail term of up to two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For the offence of not complying with a direction given by an enforcement officer to end the flight of an unmanned aircraft, to land it safely or to fly the unmanned aircraft in the manner specified by the authorised person, the Bill increases the maximum jail term from 12 months to two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Where the unmanned aircraft is operated by a person who knows that, or is reckless as to whether the unmanned aircraft operation could endanger the life or property of another person, the person may face a fine not exceeding $100,000 or a maximum imprisonment term of 10 years or both.

sections.label: Chicago Convention Annex 6 alignment
sections.summary: The Bill's Explanatory Note states the amendment aligns Singapore with Annex 6 of the Chicago Convention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Explanatory Note of the Bill states that this amendment is to put Singapore in line with Annex 6 of the Chicago Convention.

sections.label: ANA Bill drone punishments
sections.summary: The ANA Bill seeks to introduce increased punishments for illegal use of unmanned aircraft or drones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, the ANA Bill also seeks to introduce, among other things, increased punishments for illegal use of unmanned aircraft or drones.

sections.label: SAF defence against attacks
sections.summary: The speaker says he has seen tourists or foreigners use drones publicly, and received assurances that SAF can defend against attacks like those on Saudi oil installations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Like the man I saw in Sentosa, I have also seen other tourists or foreigners use such drones in the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: He gave assurances to the effect, as I understand, that SAF has the ability to defend against the kind of attacks which were levelled against the Saudi oil installations recently.

sections.label: Changi drone intrusion concerns
sections.summary: Ministerial assurances are welcome as Changi cannot afford flights affected by drone intrusions, and the speaker asks about other intrusions since June.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Any such Ministerial assurances which can be given in this respect are welcome and are important for Singapore because, for a major air hub like Changi, even if we were to exclude weaponised attacks, Changi airport cannot afford to have its flights randomly affected by drone intrusions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Senior Minister of State since the drone incidents in June causing disruptions, have there been any other incidents of drone intrusions which led to flight disruptions or nearly led to any flight disruptions?

sections.label: Flight recorder information amendments
sections.summary: The legislative amendments strengthen protection by enabling CAAS to make regulations on use or disclosure of flight recorder information, in line with Chicago Convention Annex 6 amendments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The legislative amendments are aimed at strengthening protection, by enabling CAAS to make regulations to prescribe the circumstances and appropriate safeguards under which flight recorder information can be used or disclosed, and this is in line with the latest amendments to Annex 6 of the Chicago Convention.

sections.label: Counter-unmanned aircraft measures
sections.summary: Since June 2019 there have been no intrusions affecting Changi Airport operations, and CAAS and CAG are investing in counter-unmanned aircraft measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Since June 2019, there have been no intrusions that affect the operations of Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to the Member's question on the counter-unmanned aircraft measures that we have, CAAS and CAG are investing in counter-unmanned aircraft measures to safeguard the airport.
